A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, algorithms, main sections, and Appendices A–D. Text extraction and visual inspection support a reliable comparison, including the mathematical material.

before.justification: V1 presents algorithms, theoretical guarantees, proofs, and analytical rounding examples. Neither the main text nor the appendices report original empirical results.

after.justification: V2 remains theoretical. Its added computational-cost analysis derives operation counts rather than reporting experiments, simulations, or measured runtimes.

M1.justification: Section 5 newly proposes a doubling-trick adaptation to remove the known-horizon requirement. The underlying Blum–Mansour reduction, discretization, EWOO updates, and rounding procedures in Algorithms 1–4 remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions address the same online binary-outcome calibration problem. Neither uses empirical datasets or evaluates additional tasks, populations, or environments.

E2.justification: No evaluated comparator is added or removed. The analytical comparisons with nearest-point rounding and Fishelson et al.'s rounding scheme are retained; changes in citations do not constitute new baseline evaluations.

E3.justification: Neither version specifies an empirical evaluation protocol. The added runtime analysis and unknown-horizon adaptation do not introduce experimental splits, budgets, metrics, or testing procedures.

E4.justification: No ablation, robustness test, sensitivity analysis, or empirical case study is added. The analytical example showing an Omega(1) rounding-loss increase is retained, moving from v1 Appendix C.1 to v2 Appendix C.2.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The high-probability results are theoretical concentration guarantees, and their reporting remains unchanged.

E6.justification: No measured scores, rankings, or qualitative experimental findings are added or revised. The existing regret-rate formulas in Theorems 1–3 remain unchanged; revisions to formal scope and computational derivations are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 and Proposition 2 materially narrow the L2 guarantee from a class-wide maximum to bounds for each loss, acknowledging that loss-dependent constants need not be uniformly bounded. However, Corollaries 1–2 and Appendix A.2 retain the old supremum formulations. New Appendix C.1 also derives the closed-form EWOO update and computational cost.

C1.justification: Section 1.1 narrows the novelty claim from the first sub-sqrt(T) classical l2-calibration bound to the first such high-probability bound via an efficient algorithm. The abstract's principal contributions remain unchanged, while the conclusion still claims the first high-probability and in-expectation bounds.

C2.justification: V2 adds a substantive limitation after Proposition 2: simultaneous guarantees for individual L2 losses do not necessarily control their supremum. It also explains why these individual guarantees remain meaningful for downstream decision-making; v1 lacked this qualification.

D1.justification: New Appendix C.1 explains constant-time EWOO updates using cumulative weighted outcomes, sparse power iteration for the stationary distribution, and the total cost O-tilde(T^(5/3) + T*ST). These supplement v1's pseudocode and integral expression without changing their underlying update.

R1.justification: V2 adds Foster and Hart (2023), crediting an earlier expected T^(1/3) calibration bound, and removes Roth (2022) and Roth and Shi (2024). Section 1.2 also refines the relationship to contextual omniprediction and revises its description of Okoroafor et al.'s result.

P1.justification: V2 adds a contents page and a computational-cost subsection, with localized rewrites in the introduction, related work, and Section 3.1. The overall sequence of Sections 1–7 and Appendices A–D is retained.

P2.justification: V2 separates the title/abstract from the introduction, adds a contents page, redistributes the existing algorithm boxes, and moves some displayed equations inline. Neither version contains scientific figures or result tables.

improvement.justification: V2 improves attribution, explicitly qualifies the L2 guarantee, and supplies useful implementation and cost details. The gains are limited because Corollaries 1–2 and Appendix A.2 retain the conflicting supremum claims, and the conclusion's novelty claim remains inconsistent with the added prior-work attribution. The new computational appendix also contains an incorrect gamma-function integral upper limit.
